title: What Happens When You Get Heartburn?
description:
Send this to the friend who eats dinner at 11 pm.
Heartburn isn't your heart: a muscle valve at the bottom of your food pipe relaxes and stomach acid travels up toward your throat. Your stomach has a thick mucus lining against that acid; your food pipe doesn't (Cleveland Clinic). The NHS suggests raising the head of your bed by about 10 to 20 cm (4 to 8 inches) and NOT using extra pillows, which can increase pressure on your belly and make symptoms worse. NHS: see a GP if you get heartburn most days or pharmacy medicines don't help. Call 999 (US: 911) for chest pain that spreads to your arm, neck, jaw or back, doesn't go away, or comes with sweating, feeling sick, light-headedness or shortness of breath.
Next Body File: what happens when you don't drink enough water (your pee tells on you).
